summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 58.2% YoY to INR403.5 crore and EBITDA 87.7% to INR49.2 crore, helped by China-driven dye intermediate demand.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR403.5 crore in Q2 FY27, up 58.2% YoY and 44% QoQ, with H1 at INR683.6 crore (+34.1%). EBITDA rose to INR49.2 crore at a 12.2% margin and PAT to INR35.7 crore at an 8.9% margin. Management attributed the gain to China-driven shortages of dye intermediates, Kharif-season volumes and better realisations, and commissioned Unit 5 (about 6,000 TPA dye capacity) and a 10 MW DC solar plant. The board also approved a INR70 crore new chemical plant at Unit 5 (3,000 TPA, commissioning by March 2028) funded partly by a promoter warrant issue.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 sales value INR245 crore (+85% YoY), H1 INR383 crore (+53%). Volume 14,368 MT in Q2 vs about 9,000 MT in Q1; margins lifted by Chinese dye intermediate shortages (H-Acid, vinyl sulfone price spikes).

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Q2 sales value INR158 crore (+27% YoY), H1 INR300 crore (+15%). Q2 volume about 79,000-80,000 MT; H1 about 1,45,000 MT, roughly 1-1.5% below H1 FY26 per management. Management expects Q3 to be subdued.

guidance_outlook: Management sees FY27 revenue of at least INR1,250 crore and says profitability should be in three digits (INR crore); it calls INR1,250-1,300 crore conservative.
FY28 revenue guided at about INR2,000 crore, with a 10% variation (management also cited INR1,800 crore after 10% depreciation).
Management sees scope for EBITDA and PAT margins to improve 15-20% from current levels over time, but said this is not a FY27 target.
Unit 6 trial production expected around end-Nov/Dec 2026; management is assuming no Unit 6 revenue in Q4 FY27 and full production in FY28.
Q3 FY27 chemical volumes expected to be better than Q2; Q3 fertiliser expected to be subdued due to poor season and pending subsidy announcement.
Long-term: management views current footprint as capable of 2.5-3x today's revenue once all capex completes (personal view, not guidance).
Promoter warrant balance (8,54,060 warrants at INR526.90, about INR45 crore) expected by March 2027, ahead of the June 2027 deadline.
capex_capacity: Unit 5 commercial production commenced in Q2 FY27, adding about 6,000 MT per annum of dye capacity; CFO said Unit 5 adds about 1,500 MT per quarter.
Unit 6 is mechanically complete; raw materials being imported; trial production targeted end-November or December 2026, with 3-3.5 months needed for stabilisation, approvals and NBS subsidy claim.
10 MW DC solar at Nanded commissioned; total consolidated solar capacity 20.6 MW DC.
Madhya Bharat Phosphates (wholly owned, Meghnagar, Jhabua, MP) expansion progressing; INR92 crore invested to 30 Sep 2026, funded entirely by internal accruals.

Board approved INR70 crore new chemical plant at Unit 5, Lote Parshuram: 3,000 MT per annum, commissioning by March 2028. Management estimates about INR250 crore revenue at 75% utilisation but declined to name the product.
Withdrawal of the proposed merger of Kisan and Madhya Bharat from NCLT; management said delays made it unviable.
demand_pricing: Chemical pricing firm on China dye intermediate supply gaps from environmental and safety compliance; management called H-Acid and vinyl sulfone price spikes non-sustainable and said they would normalise over weeks or months.
Management said there was no inventory gain from H-Acid, and sulfur prices are starting to ease.
Fertiliser demand supported by availability in drought-affected Maharashtra and MP; about 79,000 MT sold in Q2 despite poor rains. Central subsidy rate not yet declared (expected around 5 November).
Acid complex still running at lower levels because sulfur was high-priced and sulfuric acid could not be sold profitably.
Customer demand recovering gradually after earlier wait-and-watch; management said global demand is still somewhat weak.
Management said receivables were reviewed and are fine; realisations have risen (e.g., INR100 product now selling at INR103-110).

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 to Q2 growth between volume and realisation, and impact of global conflict.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gain was a mix of volume (Kharif peak) and realisation, with margins helped by Chinese dye intermediate shortages; Q3 fertiliser to be subdued.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 chemical sales (INR245 crore) was opportunistic from H-Acid, and what are margin prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H-Acid and vinyl sulfone price hikes are not a major driver and are not sustainable; it sees EBITDA and PAT margins better than current levels over time, but declined to quantify FY27 margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the promoter warrant money come in, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance warrant money expected before March 2027, against a June 2027 deadline, to fund Madhya Bharat expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall and was there an inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross margin fell from 32% in Q1 to 30% in Q2 (33% in Q2 FY26), attributed to inventory level changes; management denied any inventory gain.

qa_highlights.question: Next-year revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY28 revenue should be near INR2,000 crore, with about 10% variation, while FY27 is at least INR1,250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Kisan-Madhya Bharat merger withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: NCLT delays made the merger overtaken by events, so management withdrew the application as a conscious decision.

risks_watch: Chemical margins rest on temporary China-driven price spikes in H-Acid and vinyl sulfone; management itself expects normalisation.
Fertiliser H2 subdued by poor monsoon, El Nino and a pending central subsidy rate; Q3 expected weaker.
Unit 6 revenue timing uncertain: trial in Dec 2026, stabilisation and NBS/PDIL approvals may push revenue into FY28.
Management declined to disclose the product or economics of the INR70 crore Unit 5 project, and the capex-per-tonne versus Unit 5's INR37 crore raised questions.
Receivables rising and gross margin dipping QoQ were questioned; the CFO's explanation was limited.
Promoter warrant funding of about INR45 crore is pending shareholder and other approvals and is due by June 2027.
Monitor Q3 FY27 chemical volumes (management expects above 14,368 MT) and the FY27 INR1,250 crore run-rate.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the headline numbers and FY28 ambition, but guarded and deflecting on H-Acid pricing sustainability, product details of new capex, gross margin drivers and Unit 6 timing. Management repeatedly stressed being conservative while also voicing aggressive long-term targets.
key_quotes: So first of all, the margins have improved because of good demand from China in all these products.
In my opinion, if you ask me, we should be able to achieve at least INR1,250 crores of total sales and profitability should be in three digits.
Sir, if I talk about next year, like 2027-2028, in my opinion, we should be somewhere closer to near around INR2,000 crores.
Sulfur is starting to come down, and there was no inventory gain, sir.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 12.2% (vs 10% in Q2 FY26) and gross margin 30% (down from 32% in Q1), with management saying H-Acid/vinyl sulfone price spikes are non-sustainable and margin upside of 15-20% is 'over time', not a FY27 target.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 live; Unit 6 Q3-Q4 FY27
rows.why: Unit 5 (about 6,000 MT/yr, about 1,500 MT per quarter) commenced commercial production in Q2 FY27, and Unit 6 is mechanically complete with trial production targeted end-Nov/Dec 2026, though no Q4 FY27 sales are targeted.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q3 FY27 chemicals; Q3 fertiliser weak
rows.why: Q2 consolidated volume 93,645 MT (+4.3% YoY) with chemical volume 14,368 MT vs about 9,000 MT in Q1, and management expects Q3 chemical volumes above Q2, but fertiliser H1 volume is about 1-1.5% below last year and Q3 is guided subdued.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board already approved INR70 crore new chemical plant at Unit 5 (3,000 MT/yr, commissioning by March 2028) and Madhya Bharat expansion has INR92 crore invested; with Unit 6 not yet at stable run-rate, further capex is plausible but no new plan is disclosed beyond these.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management calls FY27 revenue of at least INR1,250 crore (1,250-1,300 crore) conservative, but H1 revenue is INR683.6 crore (+34.1%), so an upgrade depends on sustaining Q2's INR403.5 crore run-rate in H2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Chemical margins rest on China-driven spikes that management expects to normalise over weeks or months, Q3 fertiliser is guided subdued, and Unit 6 revenue may slip into FY28 (no Q4 FY27 sales targeted).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Unit 6 trial production targeted end-Nov/Dec 2026 with 3-3.5 months of stabilisation and approvals, and the INR70 crore Unit 5 plant (3,000 MT/yr) is due by March 2028, though the product is undisclosed.

rows.label: FY28 revenue of about INR2,000 crore (+/-10%)
rows.why: Management guides FY28 near INR2,000 crore, but this rests on Unit 6 full production in FY28 and an H1 FY27 base of INR683.6 crore, and the brief cites INR1,800 crore after a 10% haircut.

rows.label: Promoter warrant money of about INR45 crore
rows.why: Balance of 8,54,060 warrants at INR526.90 (about INR45 crore) expected before March 2027, ahead of the June 2027 deadline, to fund the Madhya Bharat expansion, though approvals are pending.

rows.label: Chemical price spikes reverse
rows.why: Management itself calls H-Acid and vinyl sulfone price spikes non-sustainable and expects normalisation over weeks or months, with sulfur prices already easing.
